family.title: The family weekend
why: Saltwater, private to your family, and fenced all the way around, with a gate. Open May to September.
Pool, grill, table and fire pit sit together behind the house, so you can cook and still see the water.
Nothing to gate off and nobody to carry up. A gas fireplace and a television for the rainy hour.
Stocked with the basics, an island for pancakes, and a dishwasher for afterwards.

near.name: Blue Ridge Tunnel (east trailhead)
near.note: Walk under the mountain: an 1850s railroad tunnel, nearly a mile long and pitch dark. Bring headlamps. It’s cool and damp inside all year.

near.name: Crabtree Falls
near.note: Big waterfalls, and the first overlook is a short walk from the parking lot. The full climb is steep, so turn back whenever the little legs say so.

near.name: Chiles Peach Orchard
near.note: Pick-your-own in season, and something sweet at the counter.

near.name: Monticello
near.note: Thomas Jefferson’s mountaintop home. Make a day of it: the house in the morning, then lunch at Michie Tavern down the hill. Book a timed ticket.

near.name: Belties
near.note: Farmhouse café on Route 151: coffee, scratch biscuits and Belted Galloway cows.

near.name: Black Bear Creamery
near.note: The reward for walking the tunnel: a cone in Nellysford, ten minutes from the house.

near.name: Blue Mountain Brewery
near.note: The easy family dinner: pizza and a big lawn in Afton, with a beer for you.

near.name: Trinacria Restaurant & Pizzeria
near.note: Pizza night, sorted: eat in, or take it home for a movie night at the house.

near.name: Brewing Tree Beer Co
near.note: Three minutes from the house. A beer for you, and a creek for the kids to splash in.

near.name: Wood Ridge Farm Brewery
near.note: A farm brewery with play equipment for the kids and a driving range for whoever still has energy. Beer for the grown-ups.

girls.title: The girls’ weekend
why: For the bride who would rather have six people and a long table than a sash and a party bus.
The king suite makes a getting-ready room: a double vanity, a soaking tub, one level, and a door that closes.
A farm table for the long sessions, a shaded porch for the afternoon ones, and a mahjong table that floats in the pool.
Tasting rooms down Route 151, a hot tub facing the ridge, a fire pit, and nobody asking you for anything.

near.name: Veritas Vineyard and Winery
near.note: A self-guided flight at your own table on a sunny deck facing the Blue Ridge, with lunch from The Terrace. The kitchen closes at 4:30, so go early.

near.name: Hazy Mountain Vineyards & Brewery
near.note: Come for the view: a glass on the hillside with the whole Blue Ridge laid out in front of you.

near.name: Afton Mountain Vineyards
near.note: 360-degree mountain views and a lake, at one of Virginia’s first farm wineries. Take a lawn table, or the glass Pavilion when it’s chilly. Snacks from home are welcome.

near.name: King Family Vineyards
near.note: A long lawn facing the mountains and one of Virginia’s best reds. Claim a table, order a bottle to share, and let the afternoon go long.

near.name: Pippin Hill Tasting Room
near.note: The pretty lunch: a long table among the vines and gardens, with a glass that matches. Book ahead on weekends.

near.name: Belties
near.note: Farmhouse café on Route 151: coffee, scratch biscuits and Belted Galloway cows.

near.name: Basic Necessities
near.note: Wine and cheese night, sorted: pick up cheese, bread and a few bottles here, then take it all back to the porch.

near.name: Greenwood Grocery
near.note: Picnic stop: made-to-order sandwiches, local cheese, bread and wine for the porch or a winery lawn.

near.name: Charlottesville Downtown Mall
near.note: Dinner in town: C&O, the Charlottesville classic just off the Downtown Mall, then a wander down the bricks. Mockingbird and Tavola are a short hop away in Belmont.

near.name: The Spa at Keswick Hall
near.note: The splurge: a massage or facial at Keswick Hall. Treatments include the steam room and infrared sauna. Book ahead.

near.name: Marigold by Jean-Georges
near.note: The splurge dinner: Jean-Georges at Keswick Hall. Dress up, and pick a driver.

game-day.title: The game weekend
why: The king suite has its own bathroom and a door that closes. The kids are at the other end of the house.
Where the game gets replayed, play by play, long after the final whistle.
A full kitchen with an island, so game day starts at home and nobody waits in line for breakfast.
Open in every season, which matters most in basketball season.

near.name: Bodo's Bagels
near.note: A Charlottesville staple. Grab a bagel on the Corner before you walk to the stadium.

near.name: Greenwood Grocery
near.note: Tailgate stop: made-to-order sandwiches, local cheese, beer and wine. On Route 250, the back way to Charlottesville.

near.name: Pro Re Nata Brewery
near.note: Halfway home on Route 250 in Crozet: a big lawn, a cold one and live music most weekends. The place to replay the game.

near.name: Duner's Restaurant
near.note: The dinner on the drive home: an old-school Ivy favorite on Route 250 with a menu that changes daily. Book on game nights.

near.name: Blue Mountain Brewery
near.note: A brewery in Afton with a kitchen, for the night you get in.

near.name: Black Bear Creamery
near.note: Ice cream in Nellysford, win or lose.

near.name: Humpback Rocks
near.note: For the morning after: a steep mile up to a rock-top view of the whole valley. It burns off the tailgate.

near.name: Boar’s Head Resort: Birdwood Golf Course and The Mill Room
near.note: If the group wants a round: Birdwood, the public course at Boar’s Head, minutes from the stadium. Then dinner at The Mill Room inside the resort.

trail151.title: The Route 151 weekend
why: The house sits in the Rockfish Valley on Route 151, so the first stop is minutes away.
A table for the bottles you bring home
A farm table and bench for six, with wine glasses in the cupboard.
For the cheese, the bread and whatever else came back with you.
A last glass by the fire
Outside at the fire pit, or inside by the gas fireplace.

near.name: Veritas Vineyard and Winery
near.note: A winery in Afton.

near.name: Afton Mountain Vineyards
near.note: A winery in Afton.

near.name: Cardinal Point Winery
near.note: A winery in Afton.

near.name: Blue Mountain Brewery
near.note: A brewery in Afton with a kitchen.

near.name: Bold Rock Hard Cider
near.note: A cidery in Nellysford.

near.name: Silverback Distillery
near.note: A distillery in Afton.

outdoors.title: The trail and snow weekend
why: Ski, tube or hike at the resort by day, then come down to a whole house, a real kitchen and your own hot tub.
The valley is your dinner menu
Barbecue, pizza, breweries and wineries along Route 151, instead of the same few places at the top of the mountain.
Open in every season, facing the ridge you were just on.
One level, and somewhere to dry out
No stairs for tired legs, a washer and dryer for wet layers, and a car port to unload under.

near.name: Blue Ridge Tunnel (east trailhead)
near.note: Walk under the mountain: an 1850s railroad tunnel, nearly a mile long and pitch dark. Bring headlamps. It’s cool and damp inside all year.

near.name: Humpback Rocks
near.note: A steep mile up to a wide view.

near.name: Ravens Roost Overlook
near.note: One of the best views on the northern Parkway: 180 degrees over the Shenandoah Valley from 3,200 feet. Go for sunset, and watch for the ravens.

near.name: Crabtree Falls
near.note: One of the tallest sets of cascades east of the Mississippi.

near.name: Wintergreen Resort
near.note: Skiing and tubing in winter, trails the rest of the year.

near.name: Devils Backbone Basecamp Brewpub
near.note: Their motto is “Drink Outdoors Together”: award-winning lagers, wood-fired food and a big meadow at the foot of the mountain. Built for trading ski and trail stories.

near.name: Iron and Ale
near.note: The step up after a hot shower: a chef-driven bistro at Stoney Creek, at the foot of Wintergreen. Book ahead on ski weekends.
